quests.sentenceWithBlank: Omar trains six days a week ____ he still struggles to lift more than he did last year.
quests.completedSentence: Omar trains six days a week yet he still struggles to lift more than he did last year.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' introduces a contrast, much like 'but,' between his intense training and his lack of progress. 'So' would wrongly imply the training caused the struggle, which reverses the real relationship.
quests.nativeTip: The struggle described goes against what you'd expect from such dedicated training.
quests.example: Omar trains six days a week yet he still struggles to lift more than he did last year.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The bank approved her loan quickly ____ she still hesitated to sign the papers.
quests.completedSentence: The bank approved her loan quickly yet she still hesitated to sign the papers.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' shows the contrast between the quick approval and her continued hesitation. 'So' would incorrectly suggest the quick approval caused her to hesitate.
quests.nativeTip: Her hesitation goes against the smooth approval, not because of it.
quests.example: The bank approved her loan quickly yet she still hesitated to sign the papers.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The kitchen renovation went over budget ____ the family had no regrets about the final result.
quests.completedSentence: The kitchen renovation went over budget yet the family had no regrets about the final result.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' fits this slightly reflective statement, expressing contrast the same way 'but' would. 'So' would wrongly imply the extra cost caused their lack of regret.
quests.nativeTip: Their positive feeling despite the extra cost is the contrast being expressed.
quests.example: The kitchen renovation went over budget yet the family had no regrets about the final result.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Liam doesn't eat meat, ____ does he eat fish.
quests.completedSentence: Liam doesn't eat meat, nor does he eat fish.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' adds a second negative idea and requires this exact inverted order - 'does he eat' - instead of the normal order 'he does eat.' 'Or' wouldn't trigger this inversion and would need different wording.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the word order after the blank - 'does he' comes before the verb, which only works with one specific connector.
quests.example: Liam doesn't eat meat, nor does he eat fish.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The manager hasn't approved the budget, ____ has she scheduled a follow-up meeting.
quests.completedSentence: The manager hasn't approved the budget, nor has she scheduled a follow-up meeting.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' correctly continues the negative idea with inversion - 'has she scheduled.' 'And' would need normal word order, 'and she hasn't scheduled,' which doesn't match this sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Again, watch the inverted verb after the blank - it signals which connector is grammatically required here.
quests.example: The manager hasn't approved the budget, nor has she scheduled a follow-up meeting.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The hotel room wasn't ready at check-in, ____ was there any apology from the staff.
quests.completedSentence: The hotel room wasn't ready at check-in, nor was there any apology from the staff.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' adds a second negative fact - no apology - using the required inverted structure. 'But' wouldn't fit this pattern and would change the meaning to contrast instead of addition.
quests.nativeTip: The verb order after the blank again points to the connector that pairs two negative ideas.
quests.example: The hotel room wasn't ready at check-in, nor was there any apology from the staff.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The candidate lacked formal qualifications ____ she impressed the panel with her practical experience.
quests.completedSentence: The candidate lacked formal qualifications yet she impressed the panel with her practical experience.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' expresses contrast in this slightly formal reflection, working the same way 'but' would. 'So' would incorrectly suggest lacking qualifications caused her to impress the panel.
quests.nativeTip: Her impressive experience contrasts with the qualification gap, not because of it.
quests.example: The candidate lacked formal qualifications yet she impressed the panel with her practical experience.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: I really wanted to come to the concert ____ I couldn't get the day off work.
quests.completedSentence: I really wanted to come to the concert but I couldn't get the day off work.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' is the natural, everyday choice for this casual message. 'Yet' would work in more formal writing, but sounds slightly stiff here.
quests.nativeTip: In casual, everyday speech like this, the more common, neutral contrast word usually fits better.
quests.example: I really wanted to come to the concert but I couldn't get the day off work.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The seeds hadn't sprouted after two weeks ____ Nina kept watering them every morning.
quests.completedSentence: The seeds hadn't sprouted after two weeks yet Nina kept watering them every morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' shows the contrast between the lack of sprouts and her continued effort. 'So' would wrongly suggest the lack of sprouts caused her watering.
quests.nativeTip: She kept up her routine despite the lack of results - that's a contrast, not a cause.
quests.example: The seeds hadn't sprouted after two weeks yet Nina kept watering them every morning.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The company didn't refund the payment, ____ did it respond to the complaint.
quests.completedSentence: The company didn't refund the payment, nor did it respond to the complaint.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' continues the negative statement with the required inversion. 'And' would need the words 'it did not respond,' not 'did it respond,' so it doesn't match this structure.
quests.nativeTip: Check the verb order after the blank again - 'did it respond' signals a specific connector for adding a second negative.
quests.example: The company didn't refund the payment, nor did it respond to the complaint.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The landlord hasn't fixed the heater ____ he says he will next week.
quests.completedSentence: The landlord hasn't fixed the heater but he says he will next week.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast vs Negative Addition - but, not nor
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' shows contrast between the unfixed heater and his promise. 'Nor' only works when the second clause is also negative and inverted, which isn't the case here.
quests.nativeTip: The second part isn't a second negative fact - it's a promise, so think about what relationship that creates.
quests.example: The landlord hasn't fixed the heater but he says he will next week.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The museum doesn't allow photography inside, ____ can visitors bring large bags.
quests.completedSentence: The museum doesn't allow photography inside, nor can visitors bring large bags.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' adds the second prohibited action using the required inversion - 'can visitors bring.' 'Or' doesn't trigger this inversion and would need rephrasing.
quests.nativeTip: Look at the inverted verb again - it's the clue for which connector continues this negative rule.
quests.example: The museum doesn't allow photography inside, nor can visitors bring large bags.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The bread hadn't risen properly ____ the baker had to start the dough again from scratch.
quests.completedSentence: The bread hadn't risen properly so the baker had to start the dough again from scratch.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' links the failed rise with the necessary result - starting again. 'And' would just list the two facts without showing why he had to restart.
quests.nativeTip: Starting over is the direct consequence of the dough not rising.
quests.example: The bread hadn't risen properly so the baker had to start the dough again from scratch.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: All the fresh produce had been sold out by noon, ____ the shelves were quickly restocked before closing.
quests.completedSentence: All the fresh produce had been sold out by noon, but the shelves were quickly restocked before closing.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' shows the shift from the produce being sold out to the shelves being restocked. 'So' would wrongly suggest the shortage caused the restocking, when it's really a separate, contrasting event.
quests.nativeTip: The restocking is a positive turn that goes against the earlier shortage, not a result of it.
quests.example: All the fresh produce had been sold out by noon, but the shelves were quickly restocked before closing.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Fans can still get tickets through the official website ____ through the box office in person, whichever is more convenient.
quests.completedSentence: Fans can still get tickets through the official website or through the box office in person, whichever is more convenient.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Or' presents the two ticket-buying options as alternatives, matching 'whichever.' 'And' would suggest fans need to use both methods together.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'whichever is more convenient' tells you this is a choice between two methods.
quests.example: Fans can still get tickets through the official website or through the box office in person, whichever is more convenient.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The volunteers hadn't received any training ____ they handled the emergency calmly and efficiently.
quests.completedSentence: The volunteers hadn't received any training yet they handled the emergency calmly and efficiently.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' expresses the contrast between the missing training and their capable response. 'Nor' wouldn't fit because the second clause is positive, not a second negative fact.
quests.nativeTip: Their calm handling goes against what you'd expect from a lack of training.
quests.example: The volunteers hadn't received any training yet they handled the emergency calmly and efficiently.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The patient doesn't have a fever, ____ does she show any other symptoms of infection.
quests.completedSentence: The patient doesn't have a fever, nor does she show any other symptoms of infection.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' continues the negative statement with the required inversion - 'does she show.' 'But' and 'yet' express contrast, not a second negative fact, and don't fit the inverted structure.
quests.nativeTip: The inverted verb order after the blank again marks this specific connector.
quests.example: The patient doesn't have a fever, nor does she show any other symptoms of infection.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Her photos weren't professionally edited ____ they still won first place in the competition.
quests.completedSentence: Her photos weren't professionally edited but they still won first place in the competition.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' fits this everyday description of the contrast. 'Nor' would only work if the second clause were also negative and inverted, which it isn't - the photos did win.
quests.nativeTip: Winning despite the lack of editing is a contrast - and here the tone is casual, not formal.
quests.example: Her photos weren't professionally edited but they still won first place in the competition.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The brakes had been checked twice before the trip ____ Sam still heard a strange noise and pulled over to have them inspected again.
quests.completedSentence: The brakes had been checked twice before the trip but Sam still heard a strange noise and pulled over to have them inspected again.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' shows that the noise occurred despite the brakes being checked twice - an unexpected outcome. 'So' would incorrectly suggest checking the brakes caused the noise.
quests.nativeTip: The noise happening despite the double-check is the contrast being expressed.
quests.example: The brakes had been checked twice before the trip but Sam still heard a strange noise and pulled over to have them inspected again.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The proposal was rejected by the board without much discussion, ____ the whole department felt discouraged for weeks.
quests.completedSentence: The proposal was rejected by the board without much discussion, so the whole department felt discouraged for weeks.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' connects the board's rejection with its emotional effect on the department. 'And' would only add the second fact without showing that the rejection caused it.
quests.nativeTip: The team's discouragement is a direct effect of the rejection, not just another added fact.
quests.example: The proposal was rejected by the board without much discussion, so the whole department felt discouraged for weeks.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Before sunset, the group can either set up camp near the river ____ push on to reach the higher ridge while there's still light.
quests.completedSentence: Before sunset, the group can either set up camp near the river or push on to reach the higher ridge while there's still light.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Or' matches the word 'either,' presenting camping and pushing on as two choices. 'And' would contradict 'either,' which signals a single choice.
quests.nativeTip: The word 'either' signals that only one of these two plans will be followed.
quests.example: Before sunset, the group can either set up camp near the river or push on to reach the higher ridge while there's still light.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The children wouldn't go to sleep ____ Grace tried reading them three different stories.
quests.completedSentence: The children wouldn't go to sleep so Grace tried reading them three different stories.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' connects the children's resistance to sleep with Grace's decision to try reading. 'And' would just add the fact without showing why she made that choice.
quests.nativeTip: Her choice to read stories is a response to the sleeping problem, not just another added fact.
quests.example: The children wouldn't go to sleep so Grace tried reading them three different stories.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Most members hadn't finished the novel by the meeting, ____ had anyone read the discussion questions in advance.
quests.completedSentence: Most members hadn't finished the novel by the meeting, nor had anyone read the discussion questions in advance.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' adds the second negative fact using the required inversion - 'had anyone read.' 'And' would need normal word order and wouldn't match this sentence as written.
quests.nativeTip: Check the inverted verb order after the blank once more - it points to the connector for adding a second negative fact.
quests.example: Most members hadn't finished the novel by the meeting, nor had anyone read the discussion questions in advance.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Her painting technique was still quite basic ____ collectors were already asking to buy her work.
quests.completedSentence: Her painting technique was still quite basic yet collectors were already asking to buy her work.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' expresses this contrast in a slightly reflective tone. 'So' would wrongly suggest her basic technique caused the collectors' interest.
quests.nativeTip: Collectors being interested despite her basic technique is the contrast at play.
quests.example: Her painting technique was still quite basic yet collectors were already asking to buy her work.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: Between meetings, Alex picked up dry cleaning ____ stopped by the pharmacy for his prescription.
quests.completedSentence: Between meetings, Alex picked up dry cleaning and stopped by the pharmacy for his prescription.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'And' links two ordinary errands he ran back to back. There's no contrast or consequence, so 'but' and 'so' don't fit.
quests.nativeTip: Both errands are simply part of the same busy afternoon, without any surprise or choice.
quests.example: Between meetings, Alex picked up dry cleaning and stopped by the pharmacy for his prescription.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: You can practice speaking with a tutor ____ complete the app's daily exercises alone - both count toward your streak.
quests.completedSentence: You can practice speaking with a tutor or complete the app's daily exercises alone - both count toward your streak.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Or' presents the tutor session and the app exercises as two separate ways to build a streak. 'And' would suggest doing both is required, which the sentence doesn't say.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'both count' tells you these are separate options, not something you must do together.
quests.example: You can practice speaking with a tutor or complete the app's daily exercises alone - both count toward your streak.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The lease clearly stated no pets were allowed ____ several tenants kept cats without any problem.
quests.completedSentence: The lease clearly stated no pets were allowed yet several tenants kept cats without any problem.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yet' fits this reflective, slightly formal contrast well. 'Nor' would only work if the second clause were also negative and inverted, which isn't the case - tenants did keep cats.
quests.nativeTip: The tone here is more like a written explanation, and the contrast is between the rule and what tenants actually did.
quests.example: The lease clearly stated no pets were allowed yet several tenants kept cats without any problem.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The new software rolled out smoothly across most departments ____ the finance team ran into constant technical problems for weeks.
quests.completedSentence: The new software rolled out smoothly across most departments but the finance team ran into constant technical problems for weeks.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'But' shows the contrast between the smooth rollout overall and finance's ongoing problems. 'So' would wrongly suggest the smooth rollout caused finance's issues, and 'nor' doesn't fit since the second clause isn't a negative statement.
quests.nativeTip: Finance's struggles are the exception here, not the outcome of the smooth rollout elsewhere.
quests.example: The new software rolled out smoothly across most departments but the finance team ran into constant technical problems for weeks.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The support team couldn't resolve the issue over the phone, ____ could they offer a clear timeline for a fix.
quests.completedSentence: The support team couldn't resolve the issue over the phone, nor could they offer a clear timeline for a fix.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Nor' continues the negative statement with the required inversion - 'could they offer.' 'So' and 'but' don't trigger this inverted structure and would change the sentence's grammar.
quests.nativeTip: The inverted verb order after the blank is your clue, just as in earlier negative-addition sentences.
quests.example: The support team couldn't resolve the issue over the phone, nor could they offer a clear timeline for a fix.

quests.sentenceWithBlank: The charity event raised far more money than expected ____ organizers immediately began planning a second event for the spring.
quests.completedSentence: The charity event raised far more money than expected so organizers immediately began planning a second event for the spring.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'So' connects the unexpectedly high funds raised with the organizers' decision to plan again. 'And' would list the two facts without showing this cause-and-effect link.
quests.nativeTip: Planning a second event is a direct response to the surprising success, not just another added fact.
quests.example: The charity event raised far more money than expected so organizers immediately began planning a second event for the spring.
